title: A Spectral Prior for Graph Coloring: Accelerating Combinatorial Search and Register Allocation
abstract: Graph coloring is a deceptively simple problem with far-reaching consequences for compiler optimization, wireless networks, and semiconductor manufacturing. Despite decades of research, widely used heuristics can perform poorly when graph structure conflicts with their greedy decision rules. A geometric prior offers a different way to guide the search toward colorings that conventional approaches may overlook. We introduce the Spherical Simplex Prior, a spectral method that uses the geometry of a regular simplex to guide graph coloring. Rather than representing color classes through circular phase variables, it distributes them across a higher-dimensional spherical geometry, providing a more balanced starting point for the search. Results on standard DIMACS challenge graphs reveal several notable behaviors: Exact coloring without search: On triangle-free Mycielski graphs with chromatic numbers of four, five, and six, the method finds optimal colorings with zero search iterations. Faster convergence: On planted flat partition graphs, where DSATUR requests twice the optimal number of colors, the method substantially reduces initial constraint violations and achieves consistent 2.09×–2.46× speedups across random seeds. Improved coloring on dense graphs: On the Queen graph queen8_8, it reaches the chromatic minimum of nine colors, using three fewer colors than DSATUR. These findings suggest that initialization geometry can matter as much as the search strategy itself. Beyond benchmark performance, the approach provides a basis for investigating how improved coloring decisions could reduce register pressure, memory traffic, and resource contention across embedded processors, enterprise CPUs, and GPUs. By connecting spectral geometry, combinatorial optimization, and computing architecture, this work explores a promising direction for improving graph-coloring heuristics and their potential impact on practical computing systems.

title: Verifier-Bound Rule Discovery: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of LLM Proposers for Combinatorial Scheduling
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as proposers of human-readable rules in scientific discovery and combinatorial optimization (FunSearch, ARCHE, SVBRD-LLM). Yet the LLM-proposer systems we surveyed share a methodological gap: none reports a same-budget random-proposer control, none pre-registers its acceptance criteria, and none evaluates at distribution scale –- ARCHE validates on three hand-picked cases, and SVBRD-LLM, the closest system to ours, is outperformed on accuracy by a black-box LSTM while reporting no significance tests. We apply a verifier-bound rule-discovery framework in which an LLM proposes interpretable rules (linear weight vectors and sandboxed programs), an independent programmatic verifier checks domain-hard properties, holdout evaluation is physically isolated and executed exactly once, and every acceptance criterion is frozen before experiments run. title: Truck Platooning—An Overview Study with Time Constraints
abstract: The truck platoon has a significant impact on modern society. As fuel costs increase daily,vehicles can be driven in a pattern to reduce fuel consumption. Vehicle routing problem is discussed in literature with taking only single objective and not considering other objectives.Multiple objectives are hard to solve.If the environment changes then vehicle routine problem gets a new route hence problem becomes challenging.In theory the data about customers and route to reach the customer will be known before but the real case scenario the request from customer changes so the environment is dynamic.The dynamic vehicle routing problem is discussed in this study with time window where which customer has to visit in what time is included.Multiple objectives such as the waiting time of the customer and minimizing routing distance to reach the customer are considered here.Hence there are multiple objectives in the dynamic environment an ensemble learning to obtain an optimization problem is discussed here ie;EL-DMOEA.Other algorithms to solve vehicle routing problem along with their comparison additionally different types of platoons, comparison of platoon with other types of the transportation is also discussed in this report.

title: The Segal-Bargmann Transform in Neural Partial Differential Equations
abstract: We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order $ L^{-\frac{1}{2}} $, where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control $ \sup_{x}\lvert\hat{u}_{NO} - u_{truth}\rvert $ for solutions of PDEs $ \mathcal{L}u = f $ which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.

title: The Informational Vector World Model (IVW): spacetime as a network of entanglement — derivations, pre-registered tests, and frozen predictions
abstract: The Informational Vector World Model (IVW) describes spacetime as a network of quantum entanglement. This combined paper contains the derivations, 42 pre-registered analyses (V07–V48, each frozen with a SHA-256 checksum before the data download or the run) and frozen predictions for future measurements. Negative results are reported in full. The central new proposal is the quenching-time relation a_0 = c H(t_q). Version 1.9, 16 October 2026. The record includes a calculation script with input data that re-computes 14 numbers of the text. All other results cannot be re-computed from this record alone. No result has yet been reproduced by others. The use of language models is disclosed in the section “Use of AI tools” of the paper. Deutsch: Das Informationelle Vektor-Weltmodell (IVW) beschreibt Raumzeit als Netzwerk aus Quantenverschränkung. Diese Gesamtarbeit enthält die Herleitungen, 42 vorregistrierte Auswertungen (V07–V48, jeweils vor dem Herunterladen der Daten oder vor dem Lauf mit einer SHA-256-Prüfsumme festgeschrieben) und die festgeschriebenen Vorhersagen für künftige Messungen. Negative Ergebnisse sind vollständig berichtet. Der zentrale neue Vorschlag ist die Abschaltzeit-Beziehung a_0 = c H(t_q). Fassung 1.9, 16. Oktober 2026. Dem Eintrag liegen ein Rechenskript mit Eingabedaten bei, das 14 Zahlen des Textes nachrechnet. Alle übrigen Ergebnisse lassen sich mit diesem Eintrag allein nicht nachrechnen. Kein Ergebnis wurde bisher von anderen nachgerechnet. Der Einsatz von Sprachmodellen ist im Abschnitt „Einsatz von KI-Werkzeugen” der Arbeit offengelegt.

title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling
abstract: Meteorological downscaling is crucial for high-resolution regional climate forecasting and disaster early warning. While neural operators have emerged as a promising paradigm for modeling complex spatiotemporal mappings, existing frameworks often struggle with spherical manifold geometric distortions, inherent atmospheric multi-scale coupling mismatches, and lack of explicit atmospheric laws. We propose the Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator, which utilizes a Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to partition atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components, maintaining exact point-wise correspondence across scales. To evaluate these representations at arbitrary locations, we introduce a localized spherical integral operator that approximates continuous kernel transforms via geometry-aware attention. Dynamical consistency is further enforced by embedding differentiable constraints into the learning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework attains superior accuracy and zero-shot generalization across various meteorological variables and unseen queries, representing a robust and interpretable solution for global-to-regional meteorological downscaling.

title: Resampling in Importance Splitting Rare Event Simulation: n-th Time’s the Charm
abstract: Abstract Importance splitting (ISPLIT) is a robust variance reduction technique that estimates the probability of rare events by decomposing the problem into a sequence of nested, easier subproblems. By partitioning the state space into regions by means of an importance function (IFUN), ISPLIT selectively clones trajectories that reach high importance layers, significantly outperforming standard Monte Carlo simulation while introducing dependencies among trajectories. Resampling (i.e., reinitializing timers given the elapsed time) can mitigate the dependency bottleneck while incurring additional computational overhead. In this paper, we empirically evaluate the impact of resampling on ISPLIT performance, investigating whether it improves estimation efficiency despite its inherent computational costs. To this end, we perform large-scale benchmarking across a variety of artificial and real-world models including queueing networks and dynamic fault trees, exploiting scalable IFUN derivation methods available in the Modest Toolset . We also discuss that resampling is implicitly performed when working with a default simulation engine in fully Markovian systems. In most cases, resampling provides a notable performance improvement, though the degree of the gain significantly depends on the model characteristics.

title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Real-time control of tokamak plasmas requires the electron density profile. However, in a reactor-relevant device, diagnostic port access is limited and the profile can be observed only partially. In the present work we reconstruct the density profile by inferring the coefficients of a physics-based one-dimensional particle transport equation, using a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) surrogate of the transport solver as a fast differentiable forward model. The surrogate enables realtime-compatible gradient-based reconstruction and uncertainty quantification from the reflectometry and interferometry measurements. We compare four uncertainty quantification methods - multi-seed ensembles, the Laplace approximation, Metropolis-Hastings, and a Gaussian method independent of the reconstruction fit. The resulting uncertainty is scored with CRPS and coverage calibration, separately on the observed and unobserved regions. We further demonstrate advantage of our approach over standard analytical function fit on synthetic and experimental DIII-D discharges.

title: QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization
abstract: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a Lagrange-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) without discretizing continuous variables. The method is based on a finite-temperature free-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p -median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target-reached rates for stringent fixed-accuracy targets. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver.

title: Neurosymbolic approach improves robustness of deep learning models for semantic segmentation of MII human oocyte images
abstract: Morphology-based assessment of metaphase II (MII) oocytes remains an important component of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) workflows, but it is affected by inter-operator variability and limited reproducibility. Deep learning approaches have shown promise for automated segmentation of oocyte structures, although purely data-driven models may generate anatomically implausible masks. Domain knowledge can instead be integrated into neural networks as explicit structural and anatomical constraints guiding training. We retrospectively analyzed 1,243 microscopic images acquired at 200× magnification from 218 patients undergoing ICSI at a single center. We propose a neurosymbolic architecture in which a logic score, derived from a set of knowledge-driven anatomical constraints, is computed on the regions of interest predicted by a transformer-based model (SegFormer). This score was used during training, alongside the segmentation loss, to guide parameter updates, and at inference as a continuous measure of morphological reliability. The neurosymbolic model was compared with an architecturally identical baseline, both quantitatively and qualitatively. To verify that the improvement is attributable to the content of the logical rules rather than to the presence of an auxiliary term, we trained two controls with identical loss form and weight but no anatomical meaning: a non-structural auxiliary loss and a scrambled rule set. The framework was further compared with U-Net and DeepLabV3+ trained on the same dataset and split, and the logic loss was additionally applied to a convolutional backbone. The neurosymbolic model achieved a macro-average intersection over union (IoU) of 0.84 and a Dice score of 0.91, outperforming the baseline (IoU 0.80; Dice 0.88), U-Net (IoU 0.76) and DeepLabV3+ (IoU 0.81). A non-structural auxiliary loss of equal weight did not reproduce this gain (IoU 0.81; Dice 0.88), and scrambling the semantics of the rules degraded performance (IoU 0.61), indicating that the improvement is driven by the content of the constraints rather than by the auxiliary term itself. By embedding domain knowledge as logical constraints, the proposed neurosymbolic framework yields more accurate and morphologically coherent segmentations of MII oocyte images than a purely neural SegFormer baseline. This approach represents a promising image-analysis component for future decision-support systems in ICSI workflows.

title: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach
abstract: Abstract Storage systems remain a significant bottleneck in large-scale deep learning training. Most evaluation studies rely on synthetic benchmarks that do not capture the I/O heterogeneity present in real training pipelines. Automated configuration methods often treat parameter selection as stateless, overlooking the temporal structure of recurring training phases. These challenges are addressed using a converged HPC-cloud platform that integrates Lustre with S3-compatible object storage. Three workloads with distinct I/O characteristics were evaluated: ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K, 3D U-Net on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and Whisper Large on LibriSpeech. Time-to-convergence was used as the primary metric. We introduced a deep reinforcement learning framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic with a Transformer-based state encoder to predict workload phase transitions rather than merely respond to them. The learned policies reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74.6% and improved GPU utilization across all three workloads. The approach generalizes across heterogeneous I/O profiles without per-workload reconfiguration. The results indicate that temporally aware storage control can improve the efficiency of distributed training pipelines in heterogeneous HPC-cloud environments.

title: AdaFuse: Adaptive Function Fusion for Dynamic Serverless Workflows
abstract: Serverless workflows are commonly modeled as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) composed of fine-grained functions. While this design promotes modularity and programming flexibility, it also incurs frequent inter-function communication. To alleviate this performance overhead, function fusion has been explored to co-locate and execute communicating functions within a shared container instance. However, existing approaches fail to account for the time-varying trade-off between communication latency reduction and resource overprovisioning arising from path uncertainty in dynamic serverless workflows, making it difficult to sustain high resource efficiency over time. In this paper, we propose a new adaptive function fusion strategy that dynamically reconstructs serverless workflows by adjusting communication schemes between functions in response to changing workflow invocations. Realizing this strategy, however, requires jointly optimizing function fusion and per-instance configuration, a problem with a combinatorial search space, while managing the substantial overhead of switching fusion schemes at runtime. To address these challenges, we design AdaFuse, a novel system for dynamic serverless workflows. AdaFuse jointly optimizes function fusion and instance reconfiguration through an efficient beam-search–based algorithm to optimize the end-to-end resource allocation. With the optimized fusion scheme, AdaFuse employs a fluid migration mechanism that incrementally transitions the workflow deployment while seamlessly redirecting incoming workloads. Evaluations across diverse benchmarks show that AdaFuse reduces resource allocation by up to 49.4% compared to baselines, without compromising SLO attainment.

title: A Review of Fault-Tolerant Reconfigurable Architectures for Autonomous Systems Based on Redundant Logic Mapping
abstract: Mission-critical applications (aerospace, automotive, and defense) have autonomous systems that must have very high reliability to allow continued operation in varied environmental structures and fault conditions. The medium of flexibility and adaptability of the computer hardware is represented by reconfigurable computing platforms and, especially, by Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Architectures (CGRAs). The review will provide an orderly research into the fault-tolerant reconfigurable architecture with an interest in redundant logic mapping which encompasses spatial, temporal, and hybrid redundancy model. We study important analysis metrics including Mean Time to Failure (MTTF), fault coverage, resources overhead and reconfiguration latency. Recent literature shows comparative results that hybrids are able to provide the MTTF with up to 3.5x scaling without a drastically high resource overhead (~2.1x LUTs, +25% power). The relevance also points to the real use in self-governing frameworks e.g. UAV, self-governing automobiles, and smart robotics, where fault cloaking, configuration abrasive, and flawless cycles are fundamental. Lastly, it presents open research issues in scalable fault diagnosis, AI-based reconfiguration as well as cross layer fault resilience, and states a guideline towards the design of next generation self-sustainable systems comprising of both economic and fault tolerant systems.

title: Trajectory Parameterization and Evolutionary Search for Constrained Optimal Control
abstract: In direct methods for constrained optimal control, accuracy depends on two things at once: the approximation space and the search applied to it. In this paper, we investigate that dependence by separating the two. A hybrid polynomial–Fourier trial space is searched by a real-coded genetic algorithm with local refinement, by a covariance-adapting evolution strategy, and by multistart of a local method, and each result is measured against the best solution the trial space itself contains. The expansion satisfies the initial conditions identically and the dynamics by construction rather than at collocation points; the control follows by inverting the dynamics, and constraints enter as blocks of algebraic rows. Nine benchmarks are solved on seven trial bases under one verification protocol, with every reference value computed here and verified independently. For the six convex problems, the best attainable value is computable, and the assisted scheme reaches it on every tested basis to a gap of at most 10−6; on the three nonconvex problems, it returns audit-admissible solutions above the feasibility threshold, under one fixed setting whose variation leaves the reported accuracy unchanged over the ranges examined. Two practical conditions are established: the trial family is over-complete and must be orthonormalized before any population-based search, and feasibility must be audited, not assumed. The accuracy attained proves not to be specific to the search: the evolution strategy reaches the same limit without local refinement, and multistart attains it on the nonconvex problems; so, what is measured is the trial space rather than the solver.

title: Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Heat-Source Inversion Estimation Method for High-Voltage Switchgear Based Reduced-Order PINN Surrogate Model
abstract: Abstract Localized overheating induced by poor electrical contact, loosened busbar connections, and insulation degradation is a major precursor to failures in high-voltage switchgear. To address the difficulty in directly measuring internal heat sources, a fast three-dimensional temperature-field reconstruction, candidate heat-source identification, and heat-source power inversion method for high-voltage switchgear is proposed based on a reduced-order surrogate model integrating Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). First, a coupled three-dimensional thermal–flow coupled computational fluid dynamics(CFD) model is established to generate temperature fields under different heat-source conditions. POD is then applied to extract the dominant thermal modes and their corresponding low-dimensional modal coefficients from the high-dimensional temperature fields. A PINN-based reduced-order surrogate model is subsequently trained to establish the nonlinear mapping from heat-source parameters to POD modal coefficients, while residuals of the steady-state heat conduction equation and boundary-condition constraints are incorporated into the loss function to enforce physical consistency and enhance prediction accuracy. Based on external temperature measurements, an Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (I-GWO) is further adopted to identify the active fault heat source from a predefined set of candidate locations and inversely estimate its corresponding heat-source power. Numerical simulations and temperature-rise experiments show that the proposed method accurately reconstructs the three-dimensional temperature distribution and identifies local high-temperature regions. In the temperature-rise experiment, the relative error of heat-source power inversion is only 2.27%, demonstrating that the proposed framework enables rapid and accurate temperature-field reconstruction and heat-source inversion.

title: Reinforcement learning to disentangle multiqubit quantum states from partial observations
abstract: Using partial knowledge of a quantum state to control multiqubit entanglement is a largely unexplored paradigm in the emerging field of quantum interactive dynamics with the potential to address outstanding challenges in quantum state preparation and compression, quantum control, and quantum complexity. We present a deep reinforcement learning (RL) approach using an actor-critic algorithm for constructing short disentangling circuits for states with up to 16 qubits. With access to only two-qubit reduced density matrices, our agent decides which pairs of qubits to apply two-qubit gates on; requiring only local information makes it directly applicable on modern NISQ devices, as we demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum computer. Utilizing a permutation-equivariant transformer architecture, the agent can autonomously identify qubit permutations within the state, and adjusts the disentangling protocol accordingly. Once trained, it provides circuits from different initial states without further optimization. We demonstrate the agent's ability to identify and exploit the entanglement structure of multi-qubit states. We analyze the disentangling circuits constructed by the agent for 4- and 5-qubit Haar-random states, and observe strong correlations between consecutive gates and among the qubits involved. Through extensive benchmarking, we show the efficacy of the RL approach to find disentangling protocols with minimal gate resources. We explore the resilience of our trained agents to noise, highlighting their potential for real-world quantum computing applications. Analyzing optimal disentangling protocols, we report a general circuit to prepare an arbitrary 4-qubit state using at most 5 two-qubit (10 CNOT) gates.

title: Physics-informed neural operators for rapid electric field prediction in transcranial magnetic stimulation of healthy and tumor subjects
abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-induced electric fields is essential for personalized clinical applications, from individualized therapy in major depressive disorder to presurgical functional mapping in neuro-oncology. Yet conventional finite element methods are often too computationally expensive for interactive use. Existing deep learning surrogate models partly address this limitation but are largely constrained to fixed voxel-grid representations that cannot naturally accommodate the irregular geometry of subject-specific head meshes. We present the first physics-informed neural operator (PINO) for subject-specific prediction of vector TMS electric fields, built on a mesh-native dual-encoder architecture that jointly encodes head anatomy and coil configuration. By incorporating a curl-based regularization term aligned with the curl-free nature of the TMS secondary field, the PINO model promotes physical consistency as a soft regularizer alongside data-driven supervision. Trained on 75 subjects from the IXI dataset, the framework was evaluated across four independent held-out test datasets, including healthy subjects from two additional MRI cohorts and, for the first time in learning-based TMS electric-field prediction, tumor patients. The resolution-agnostic formulation generalizes across subjects, coil types, and spatial resolutions without retraining, predicting vector electric fields on approximately 300,000 gray matter volume nodes in under 100 ms on a consumer-grade GPU. Across all test datasets within the focality-50% region, the PINO model achieved median center-of-gravity errors of 0.39–0.43 mm, RMSE of 0.12–0.16 V/m, and mean angular deviations of 6.7°–7.3°, with performance within or below the error ranges reported by recent deep-learning approaches. At the selected 5% physics-loss weighting, curl loss decreased by 9.1% relative to the data-only model, while RMSE and MAD increased by only 1.6% and 1.3%, respectively. These results suggest that physics-informed neural operators provide a scalable technical foundation for rapid gray-matter electric-field approximation, supporting future studies on real-time electric-field-guided TMS workflows

title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
abstract: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. Water scarcity and pollution threaten human health, economic development and environmental sustainability. Traditional water treatment methods do not generally achieve effective removal of emerging pollutants and pathogen. Thus, the properties of nanomaterials at the molecular scale make it unique, and open new possibilities for development of more efficient, cost effective and environmentally friendly water purification. Nanotechnology is changing the way we clean and reuse water resources from nano adsorbents that remove toxic metals selectively and nanomembranes that filter out the slightest contaminants. In this article we will look at the advances in nanomaterials for water purification looking at how they work, what they are good for, and they could help enlighten us about the global water crisis. Through these innovations we’ll explore ways these are redefining the future of water management for anyone and everyone, not just industries and communities, but all across the globe.

title: Look Before You Act: Bridging Active Perception and Vision-Language-Action Models via Observation-Aligned Data Adaptation
abstract: Robots manipulating objects in clutter must decide not only how to act, but also where to look. Although active camera motion can expose an occluded target, it may move the robot into an initial observation-state distribution that differs from the manipulation policy's training distribution. We identify this problem as first-frame distribution sensitivity: under perturbed starts in LIBERO, naively prepending camera repositioning to pi_0.5 reduces success from 46.3% to 11.5%. We introduce ActiveAlign, a data-adaptation framework that trains a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy from the states at which active perception terminates. A learned viewpoint module first generates a camera trajectory. Offline, ActiveAlign uses closed-loop alignment to connect the trajectory endpoint to an existing demonstration, replays the remaining manipulation trajectory, and retains successful continuations for fine-tuning. At deployment, the same viewpoint module precedes the adapted VLA without modifying its architecture. Across 40 LIBERO tasks, ActiveAlign achieves 70.7% success with pi_0 and 72.7% with pi_0.5, outperforming their standard-training baselines by 40.0% and 26.4% respectively. Matched-state and data-matched controls support gains beyond prefix shortening and generic viewpoint augmentation; OpenVLA and GR00T N1 also show the same trend. Success rate under physical occlusion in real world increases from 35/90 to 83/90. These results show that active perception benefits manipulation when policy training is aligned with the observation and robot-state distribution induced by viewpoint selection.

title: Learning Structure to Support Autonomous Control Decisions
abstract: Autonomous systems have been the subject of substantial consequential research, with applications ranging from space exploration to self-driving vehicles. In unstructured and novel environments, such systems must make control decisions under partial observability, where sensing is noisy and incomplete and dynamics are uncertain or imperfectly modeled. Issues stemming from partial observability and uncertainty can be mitigated using predictive models that summarize an agent's past experiences; that is, mechanisms capable of anticipating the outcomes of the agent's (or even other agents') decisions and actions. This dissertation develops exploration methods for learning transition models of controllable interactions between a robot and its environment and evaluates how these learned models improve planning under uncertainty. Such planning capabilities, in turn, support agents in sequential decision making, as well as in active information gathering purposes aimed at reducing uncertainty while reaching desirable states and avoiding unrecoverable failures. This dissertation specifically investigates the challenge of learning a model of an agent's transition function, which encodes a probability distribution over outcome states that may occur when an action is performed at a given state. These models support agents in reasoning over trajectories of (open or closed loop) controlled state transitions in order to solve various types of tasks. Furthermore, we study mechanisms to learn such models through autonomous exploration in a way that addresses issues of exploration efficiency, ability of learned models to solve downstream tasks, accuracy of models in describing dynamics, and completeness of models in fully representing entire state-action spaces. We introduce two novel methods for autonomously exploring partially observable environments in order to efficiently build predictive models. These exploration processes leverage information theoretic measures that capture model-learning progress based on how much dynamics model estimates change during interaction. We also investigate various metrics to quantify these changes, such as the magnitude of entropy change and the Kullback-Leibler divergence between successive model estimates. The first algorithm we propose, Intrinsically Motivated Structure Learning, greedily maximizes learning progress and thereby efficiently guides exploration toward actions where the estimated transition model does not match reality. The second algorithm, Acquisition of Salient Control Knowledge, identifies effective exploration and information gathering behaviors by planning over a fixed horizon and leveraging currently estimated models to balance exploration and exploitation, thereby enabling more rapid construction of accurate and complete predictive models. We show that these algorithms converge to stable and accurate model estimates using fewer actions than baseline approaches. We then evaluate the impact of the learned models by quantifying the quality and performance of autonomous agent behaviors when solving novel tasks through model-based planning in belief space. The tasks in which we evaluate our techniques represent settings in which an agent faces incomplete information and must actively select actions to mitigate uncertainty by using its models. We show that models learned through our methods support decision making that actively reduces uncertainty and enables agents to solve families of tasks with fewer actions and higher success rates than existing techniques.

title: LangNCO: Compiling Natural-Language Constraints into Inference-Time Interventions for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) rapidly produces high-quality solutions for problem structures encountered during training, but operational requirements may change after deployment and be communicated in natural language. We propose LangNCO, a framework that compiles instance-specific requirements into structured inference-time interventions for a frozen NCO solver, without changing the pretrained policy's architecture, learned input representation, or parameters. A pretrained LLM serves as a replaceable semantic front end, translating each requirement into a schema-validated domain-specific language (DSL) rule set. A deterministic Rule Executor applies the rules as nonexpansive hard action masks. Because local masking prevents immediate violations but does not ensure that a complete feasible continuation remains reachable, Critical-Offset Decoding extracts rule-referenced critical nodes and reallocates part of a fixed rollout budget to multi-strength biased rollouts. Using controlled task-specific language to isolate solver adaptation from open-ended language robustness, we evaluate a CVRP policy on road closures, time windows, vehicle assignments, visit-order requirements, all pairwise combinations, and twelve additional constraint types. LangNCO achieves 100% feasibility on the four primary datasets with mean reference gaps of 1.63--3.26%, 97.33--100% feasibility when separately generated rules are composed for pairwise constraints, and 98.67% feasibility across the additional constraints. These results demonstrate modular post-training adaptation of a frozen NCO solver through inspectable language-derived rules, without retraining.

title: LAW: Unifying Language, Action, and World Modeling for Agentic Physical Intelligence
abstract: World-action models jointly predict actions and future world states, but long-horizon manipulation further requires language reasoning to plan subtask objectives, assess execution progress, and guide action selection. We present LAW, a closed-loop VLM--WAM framework that unifies language reasoning, action generation, and world modeling through semantic subtask progress. Within the LAW agent, a hybrid-expert vision-language model plans the remaining subtasks, estimates the values of and fuses actions proposed by a world-action model, and asynchronously assesses execution status to support continued execution and subtask transitions. Within the world-action model, Mixture-of-Transformer Experts integrates modality-specific and shared computation for joint video--action modeling. Dual-stream hierarchical visual memory maintains temporal context for both models, while subtask-local value learning aligns action evaluation with semantic objectives and preserves supervision from successful prefixes of failed trajectories. LAW achieves 94.21% average success across 50 RoboTwin tasks. Replacing the WAM backbone with OpenWAM-$alpha$ further raises the average success rate to 95.56%, establishing a new open-source state of the art on RoboTwin. Despite having only 2B parameters, our VLM also outperforms variants using Embodied-R1.5 and GPT-5.5 High. On three long-horizon real-robot tasks, LAW achieves 65% average success, compared with 28.33% for $pi_{0.5}$ and 25% for Fast-WAM.

title: Hybrid modeling of grounding and collision risk for vessels not under command
abstract: Although loss of control (not under command, NUC) is one of the leading triggers of maritime accidents, the quantitative role of human and organizational factors in the process by which it evolves into a risk of grounding and collision has been largely neglected. Traditional approaches primarily treat this situation as a technical reliability issue; however, whether a loss of control leads to a disaster is often determined not by the failure itself, but by human and organizational performance in the first few minutes following the failure. To address this gap, this study proposes an original hybrid methodological framework that combines LLM-supported HFACS-PV coding, Monte Carlo simulation, and decision tree analysis within a sequential and integrated data flow. Within this framework the predictive and quantitative burden rests on the Monte Carlo simulation, while the decision tree contributes an interpretable, descriptive account of factor combinations; it is not presented as a validated predictive classifier. NUC cases compiled from publicly available accident investigation reports were coded into five HFACS-PV layers using a large language model-supported protocol; the resulting layer load was converted into a human factor multiplier that scales the vessel’s time to regain power and fed into the probabilistic simulation as input. The simulation predicts the likelihood of catastrophic outcomes following a loss of control and highlights how the critical time window for intervention narrows significantly—particularly in extreme scenarios—emphasizing the decisive role of initial response capacity. A controlled sensitivity analysis shows that, when physical variables are held constant, the human factor significantly alters the probability of a catastrophic event; however, this effect acts as a conditional modulator dependent on the available time window. Decision tree analysis reveals that the simultaneous occurrence of technology–interface failures and skill-based errors is the pattern most strongly associated with catastrophic outcomes. This decision-tree finding is descriptive and exploratory in nature; under leave-one-out cross-validation the model does not outperform the majority-class baseline and is therefore not used as a predictive classifier. Furthermore, deficiencies in organizational processes and safety management systems emerged as the dominant latent condition in the vast majority of cases, and independent cases outside the dataset also confirmed this trend. The proposed framework offers a practical and comparative decision-support tool that integrates text-based human factor analysis with probabilistic risk modeling.

title: Enhancing Visual Task-Redirection Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models via Closed-Loop Optimization
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable language-guided robot manipulation, but remain vulnerable to visual attacks that undermine user control over robot behavior. Prior studies optimize visual perturbations using fixed target supervision. However, the perturbation can change earlier actions and, in turn, the physical states reached later. As the attacked trajectory evolves, this supervision may no longer match the behavior needed at the states actually reached. Accurately matching these targets can therefore fail to advance the attacker-specified task. Even with suitable supervision, reducing average matching error does not ensure sustained task progress. The robot may still fail at a critical stage, and further updates can disrupt previously successful behavior. To address these limitations, we propose TRACO, a framework that enhances existing targeted visual attacks through closed-loop optimization. Its Execution-Driven Supervision rebuilds supervision for the states reached under attack to guide subsequent updates. Within this framework, Progress-Guided Selection focuses updates where progress stalls while maintaining supervision on the earlier behavior needed to reach that point. Experiments across VLA models and simulation environments show improved task-redirection success with TRACO, highlighting the security implications of closed-loop attack optimization.

title: Edge-native Small Language Models for 6G Intent-driven Slicing: A Hardware-grounded Empirical Study
abstract: This study presents a deterministic, hardware-grounded empirical evaluation of open-weight Small Language Models (SLMs) on CPU-only edge infrastructure.Using greedy decoding for exact reproducibility, we benchmark four ∼8B-parameter families (Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 2, GLM-4) under identical Q4_K_M quantisation, then run a 4×3 scaling analysis of Qwen 2.5 (0.5B-7B).By capturing validated telemetry-RAPL (Running Average Power Limit) package energy and IMC (Integrated Memory Controller) DRAM bandwidth across NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) nodes-we provide direct hardware evidence of a memory-bandwidthsensitive regime for SLM edge inference.The results reveal a trade-off: Gemma 2 9B attains the highest actioncorrectness (50.0%, p=0.0037), while Qwen 2.5 7B is more efficient (2.1× faster, 2.3× lower marginal energy).We identify Qwen 2.5 3B (Q4_K_M) as the accuracy-efficiency sweet spot: 46.0% action accuracy, 5.1 s/intent, 1,997 MB peak memory, statistically tied with its 7B counterpart under identical Q4_K_M quantisation (McNemar p=0.11).

title: Does the additional attraction of a dwarf galaxy depend on its history? A pre-registered test of the quenching-time relation on 51 dwarf galaxies
abstract: Does the additional attraction of a dwarf galaxy depend on its history? A pre-registered test of the quenching-time relation on 51 dwarf galaxies. Version 1.5, 16 October 2026. The Informational Vector World Model (IVW) predicts that dwarf galaxies which stopped forming stars early show a larger velocity dispersion than a law without memory allows. The prediction was fixed in writing before the evaluation (pre-registered, SHA-256 checksums kept within the project, no external timestamp). On 51 dwarf galaxies the pre-registered criterion is met: 2ΔlnL = +32.3 (threshold 9), slope 1.47 ± 0.26. The paper then looks for reasons not to believe this. The particular form of the relation is not supported: with the same number of parameters a simple linear dependence on the quenching time fits better, and under the relation this happens in 4 of 4000 simulations. The signal rests mainly on the difference between gas-rich and gas-free dwarfs, and three known biases that enlarge this difference are not corrected for. After the result, the signal also turns out to be degenerate with luminosity: absolute magnitude alone explains the data far better than the quenching time (+67.1 against +25.3), and a paired test at equal luminosity, fixed in advance, cannot decide (0.46 ± 0.46; about 50 new pairs would be needed). The paper states what it does not show. The question whether the additional attraction depends on history or only on luminosity stays open. Files: the paper in English and German (PDF), the computation script in both languages (74 checks against the numbers of the text, runtime one to two minutes), the two input tables, README and requirements. License: CC BY 4.0. Generative language models (Anthropic Claude) were utilized as supportive tools for grammatical refinement, code verification, and literature research. All theoretical derivations, mathematical calculations, data analyses, and scientific evaluations were conducted independently by the author, who assumes full responsibility for the content. --- Hängt die Zusatzanziehung einer Zwerggalaxie von ihrer Geschichte ab? Ein vorregistrierter Test der Abschaltzeit-Beziehung an 51 Zwerggalaxien. Fassung 1.5, 16. Oktober 2026. Das Informationelle Vektor-Weltmodell (IVW) sagt voraus, dass Zwerggalaxien, die früh aufgehört haben, Sterne zu bilden, eine größere Geschwindigkeitsstreuung zeigen, als ein Gesetz ohne Gedächtnis erlaubt. Die Vorhersage wurde vor der Auswertung schriftlich festgelegt (vorregistriert, SHA-256-Prüfsummen nur innerhalb des Projekts hinterlegt, ohne externen Zeitstempel). An 51 Zwerggalaxien ist das vorab festgelegte Kriterium erfüllt: 2ΔlnL = +32,3 (Schwelle 9), Steigung 1,47 ± 0,26. Danach sucht die Arbeit selbst nach Gründen, dem nicht zu glauben. Die besondere Form der Beziehung wird nicht gestützt: Bei gleicher Parameterzahl passt eine einfache lineare Abhängigkeit von der Abschaltzeit besser, und unter der Beziehung kommt das in 4 von 4000 Simulationen vor. Das Signal ruht vor allem auf dem Unterschied zwischen gasreichen und gasfreien Zwergen, und drei bekannte Verzerrungen, die diesen Unterschied vergrößern, sind nicht herausgerechnet. Nach dem Ergebnis zeigt sich außerdem, dass das Signal mit der Leuchtkraft entartet ist: Die absolute Helligkeit allein erklärt die Daten weit besser als die Abschaltzeit (+67,1 gegen +25,3), und ein vorab festgelegter Paartest bei gleicher Leuchtkraft kann nicht entscheiden (0,46 ± 0,46; etwa 50 neue Paare wären nötig). Die Arbeit benennt, was sie nicht zeigt. Ob die Zusatzanziehung von der Geschichte abhängt oder nur von der Leuchtkraft, bleibt offen. title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
abstract: We address the problem of improving the performance of pre-stabilized networked systems subject to plug-and-play (PnP) operations, namely additions or removals of subsystems. While distributed baseline controllers can preserve stability after a PnP transition, augmenting them with expressive neural policies can invalidate the formal stability guarantees. To overcome this issue, we build on recently proposed Performance Boosting controllers based on the Internal Model Control (IMC) principle, which reduce closed-loop stability to a finite $\ell_2$-gain requirement on an auxiliary operator. In the distributed setting, this operator is formed by interconnecting local neural operators that exchange information only between neighboring subsystems. We then derive free parametrizations of this interconnection, namely explicit maps from unconstrained trainable variables to interconnected neural operators satisfying a prescribed network gain bound for every parameter value. The obtained distributed neural controller can therefore be trained by unconstrained gradient-based optimization without stability constraints or projection steps, while retaining the prescribed gain bound at every training iterate. We develop two complementary parametrizations. A neighbor-based compositional parametrization uses local coupling bounds, so that after a PnP event only subsystems whose bounds change need to update their gain parameters. A network-norm parametrization instead uses a bound on the overall coupling matrix and can reduce conservatism, at the price of requiring network-wide information. A PnP DC-microgrid case study shows that the proposed neural layer improves voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.

title: Decoupled Entropic-Geometric Planning (DEGP): Verified Conditioning and a Measured Contact-Prediction Boundary in Latent World Models
abstract: Gradient-based latent space planning faces a fundamental trade-off: maintaining high-entropy representations for robust perception under domain shift often yields ill-conditioned manifolds that destabilize trajectory optimization. DEGP introduces a framework designed to isolate gradient interference between representation learning and control dynamics via strict architectural separation. However, empirical evaluation demonstrates that structural decoupling alone is insufficient for closed-loop planning (0/50 per condition; 0/200 total), uncovering a fundamental information-usability gap driven by contact-conditional predic-tion errors and cost signal suppression. The gap is not closed by retraining the encoder to be more decodable: a trained encoder whose T-pose decodability matches DEGP’s (R2=0.686) still yields a predictor that captures essentially no contact-conditioned movement (CDR = 0.046, versus the frozen random encoder’s 0.060). To delineate these operational limits, we provide analytical proofs establishing guaranteed spectral bounds on the predictor’s Ja-cobian under distribution shifts. Furthermore, we validate DEGP across manipulation tasks, ntroducing a telemetry-based runtime contract that quantifies the operational boundaries where geometric conditioning preserves planning stability.

title: Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform
abstract: Neural networks whose inputs are functions, as in operator learning, are usually shown to be universal by existence arguments, either by reduction to finite-dimensional networks or by Stone--Weierstrass-type density; these prove that approximants exist but say little about how the parameters depend on the target. We take a constructive route. We extend the ridgelet transform, an integral transform related to the Fourier, Radon, and wavelet transforms, to continuous maps on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, replacing the Lebesgue measure that is unavailable in infinite dimensions by Gaussian weights with a homogeneous mixture on the direction space. The resulting transform has a Plancherel identity and reconstruction formulas incorporating the frame operator, the correction induced by the weights, and it assigns to each target an explicit coefficient measure, one for every admissible analysis filter. From these representations we obtain uniform approximation on compact sets for all continuous non-polynomial activations of polynomial growth, including ReLU, and, by Monte Carlo sampling of the coefficient, finite-width networks with a dimension-free $O(N^{-1/2})$ error in the width $N$ for globally Lipschitz activations and coefficients with finite variation and second moments. Explicit examples include Gaussian targets and neural-operator layers. A companion Lean~4 formalization provides machine-checked proofs, with its correspondence to the manuscript documented at https://shosonoda.github.io/lean-operator-ridgelet/ .

title: Conformalized Quantum DeepONet Ensembles: Towards Scalable Operator Learning with Distribution-Free Guarantees
abstract: Abstract Operator learning enables fast surrogate modelling of high-dimensional dynam-ical systems, but existing approaches face two fundamental limitations: the quadratic cost of dense neural layers and unreliable uncertainty quantification in safety-critical settings. We propose Conformalized Quantum Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) Ensembles, a framework that addresses both challenges simultaneously. Using Quantum Orthogonal Neural Networks (QOrthoNNs), we characterize the resource regime in which their established˜︁established˜︁ O(n) hidden-layer running-time scaling improves on the O(n 2) cost of a classical dense layer. To quantify uncertainty, we combine ensemble predictions with split conformal calibration. For a new input–output function pair jointly exchangeable with the calibration pairs, we prove a finite-sample, distribution-free lower bound on the expected fraction of covered query locations. As a secondary proof-of-concept, we explore hybrid classical–quantum architectures and superposed execution to manage ensemble runtime and hardware requirements. Experiments on synthetic operator benchmarks and real-world power-system dynamics show accurate predictions under ideal simulation and empirical coverage near the target under both ideal conditions and selected compact-circuit simulations with depolarizing 1 or device-calibrated composite noise. Together, these results connect resource-aware scalability analysis with finite-sample uncertainty guarantees for quantum operator learning.

title: Caputo-inspired Adaptive Genetic Algorithm and Taguchi Design of Experiment to Solve Capacitated Ambulance Routing Problem
abstract: This study proposes an adaptive genetic algorithm based on a nabla Caputo fractional difference with the Taguchi design of experiment for solving the capacitated ambulance routing problem.The optimization problem considered aims to minimize the total ambulance routing cost while satisfying ambulance availability and capacity.In this study, a nabla Caputo fractional difference-based adaptive mutation mechanism is designed and incorporated into the genetic algorithm evolutionary process.This so-called memory-aware mechanism captures historical fitness behavior and is used as an adaptive control signal for dynamically adjusting the mutation rate during optimization.To obtain appropriate parameter settings systematically, the Taguchi design of experiment is employed in two stages.The first stage tunes the genetic algorithm parameters, such as the maximum number of generations, the population size, and the fixed mutation rate.While the second stage tunes the nabla Caputo fractional-memory parameters, such as the fractional order, the memory window, the scaling coefficient, and the maximum adaptive mutation rate.The proposed algorithm is interpreted through the lens of nonlinear dynamical systems.For the performance evaluation, this study uses Augerat benchmark instances.The results show that the proposed algorithm is competitive against established hybrid metaheuristics.These findings suggest that integrating the nabla Caputo fractional-memory dynamics with statistically guided parameter tuning offers a promising solution for the capacitated ambulance routing problem.

title: CA-VSN: A Context-aware Variable Selection Network with Context-guided Cross-attention for Personalized Recommendation
abstract: Providing personalized recommendations, depends on two complementary sources of information, one is user's past interactions and the second is the context in which a new decision is made.In practice, however, combining these two sources is not straightforward.Many existing methods either treat contextual variables too uniformly which introduces context noise.The context noise weakens personalization as user history is utilized without adequately accounting for the current context at hand.To address this problem, this paper proposes CA-VSN, a Context-Aware Variable Selection Network for highly personalized recommendation.The model first uses a Variable Selection Network to assign instance-specific importance weights to contextual variables and build a refined context representation.It then applies a Context-Gated Cross-Attention mechanism, where the refined context vector is used to retrieve the most relevant signals from the user's historical interactions.A gating function further controls how strongly historical information should influence the prediction under the current context.CA-VSN is evaluated on ITM-Rec and MovieLens-100K for both rating prediction and Top-K recommendation.CA-VSN remains competitive in both score prediction and ranking with Recall@20 = 0.831 and NDCG@20 = 0.460 on ITM-Rec and Recall@20 = 0.705 and NDCG@20 = 0.383 on MovieLens-100K.Additional ablation and sensitivity analyses confirm the importance of the proposed components and the robustness of the model design.Beyond predictive performance, CA-VSN provides inspectable feature selection and history attention signals whose behavioural relevance is supported by perturbation, stability, and counterfactual analyses.Refining context before modelling history offers an effective approach to personalized recommendation.

title: Autonomous AI for Electronic Design Automation (AI-EDA): Reinforcement Learning Floorplanning, Graph Neural Routing, and Sub-2nm PPA Optimization
abstract: Modern Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) semiconductor design is confronting unprecedented computational complexity as leading-edge manufacturing descends into sub-2nm Gate-All-Around (GAA) nanosheet nodes and 3D heterogeneous chiplet packaging. System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures integrating over 100 billion transistors exhibit hyper-dimensional search spaces exceeding 10^{2500} potential macroscopic placement and routing configurations. Traditional Electronic Design Automation (EDA) flows rely on manual, iterative engineering cycles and heuristic combinatorial algorithms (e.g., Simulated Annealing, Force-Directed Placement, and A* maze routing) that require multi-month turnaround times and struggle to converge within stringent Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) margins. Autonomous AI-driven EDA establishes a transformative paradigm shift: replacing manual heuristic floorplanning and layout iterations with end-to-end Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents, Spatial Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), and differentiable surrogate physics models. However, deploying deep learning models within sub-2nm chip design flows introduces severe structural and physical bottlenecks: high-dimensional graph scale explosions on multimillion netlist graphs, severe Design Rule Check (DRC) violations under extreme ultraviolet (EUV) photolithography constraints, non-differentiable Static Timing Analysis (STA) loops, and complex parasitic RC wire delays. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of autonomous AI-EDA architectures. We formalize chip placement as a constrained Markov Decision Process (MDP), model congestion and wirelength estimation using Heterogeneous Hypergraph Neural Networks (H-GNNs), and formulate differentiable analytical placement via Electrostatic Charge Analogy formulations (e-Place / DreamPlace). Furthermore, we construct an enterprise physical design testbed across open-source and commercial tapeout netlists (OpenROAD, RISC-V SoC cores, and industrial GPU microarchitectures) under 7nm, 3nm, and 2nm GAA process design kits (PDKs). Our empirical results demonstrate that our deep reinforcement learning and hypergraph placement engine reduces Total Negative Slack (TNS) by 64.2%, slashes routing wirelength by 14.8%, and accelerates physical floorplanning turnaround times from weeks to 5.4 hours while achieving zero DRC violations. Finally, we formulate open research directions in all-neural static timing engines, 3D monolithic inter-tier thermal modeling, and foundation models for hardware description language (HDL) logic synthesis.

title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems
abstract: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity (resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high-dimensional fluid flows and a real-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input–output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.

title: A hybrid metaheuristic for the family capacitated vehicle routing problem
abstract: Abstract The Family Traveling Salesman Problem (FTSP) seeks a minimum-cost tour from a depot that visits a prescribed number of members of each customer family. This paper studies the Family Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (F-CVRP), a generalization of the FTSP in which customers carry demands and are served by a homogeneous fleet of capacitated vehicles, and proposes a hybrid metaheuristic for it. The method, named ILS+SP, couples an Iterated Local Search (ILS), which embeds a Random Variable Neighborhood Descent (RVND) over classical and problem-specific neighborhoods and accepts worsening moves through a Simulated-Annealing criterion, with a Set Partitioning (SP) post-optimization over the pool of routes collected during the search. On 144 large benchmark instances with more than 50 nodes, the metaheuristic wins or ties on every instance against the state-of-the-art heuristic of the literature, reducing the average gap to the best known solution from 1.84 to 0.01%. On a new benchmark of 120 larger instances with up to 142 customers, it attains an average gap of $$0.47\%$$ 0.47 % to the best solutions found across all our runs, within an average total running time of 37 s (a 20-second ILS budget plus the Set Partitioning post-optimization), showing that the method scales to these instance sizes in terms of running time.

title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer semantic knowledge acquired through vision-language pretraining to robot control, achieving strong performance across various benchmarks. However, most VLAs directly map observations to demonstrated actions without explicit supervision of intermediate physical state changes, making them prone to overfitting observation-action correspondences. Some methods introduce intermediate reasoning or future-state prediction in language, visual, or latent spaces to guide action generation, but do not explicitly supervise the physical state transition itself. We therefore propose VLA-$Δ$, a general framework that uses physical changes between current and future states as explicit learning targets. To support this objective, we construct a large-scale pretraining dataset and derive physical state-transition annotations covering task-relevant semantics and visual motion changes, providing more direct supervision for continuous action generation. During inference, the model generates actions directly from current observations without additional inference overhead. VLA-$Δ$ achieves performance competitive with the state of the art on LIBERO and RoboTwin, and outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in real-robot experiments. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-OmniAI/VLA-Delta

title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection
abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of cancer risk from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) could support earlier detection and improved care, but modeling such complex patient trajectories remains challenging. We present TrajOnco, a training-free, multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework designed for scalable multi-cancer early detection. Using a chain-of-agents architecture with long-term memory, TrajOnco performs temporal reasoning over sequential clinical events to generate patient-level summaries, evidence-linked rationales, and predicted risk scores. We evaluated TrajOnco on de-identified Truveta EHR data across 15 cancer types using matched case-control cohorts, predicting risk of cancer diagnosis at 1 year. In zero-shot evaluation, TrajOnco achieved AUROCs of 0.64–0.80, performing comparably to supervised machine learning in a lung cancer benchmark while demonstrating better temporal reasoning than single-agent LLMs. The multi-agent design also enabled effective temporal reasoning with smaller-capacity models such as GPT-4.1-mini. The groundedness of TrajOnco’s output was supported by human evaluation. Furthermore, TrajOnco’s interpretable reasoning outputs can be aggregated to reveal population-level risk patterns that align with established clinical knowledge. These findings highlight the potential of multi-agent LLMs to execute interpretable temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHRs, advancing both scalable multi-cancer early detection and clinical insight generation.

title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.

title: TS-WAM: Temporal Latent Actions and World-Action Coupling for Vision-Language Robot Control
abstract: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. We present TS-WAM, a lightweight Teacher-Student World-Action Model that addresses these challenges through self-supervised temporal learning and explicit future prediction. Its vlm-jepa framework learns from heterogeneous data, including robot demonstrations and action-free human videos, using an EMA target branch without requiring a separately trained external teacher. By coupling vlm-jepa with delta-lwm, TS-WAM learns to predict latent actions from the current observation and instruction and uses them to predict future visual features that guide action generation at inference. A unified end-to-end training architecture jointly optimizes temporal representation learning, visual dynamics, and robot control without a separate latent-action or world-model pretraining stage. The EMA target branch is removed at inference, keeping the deployed policy lightweight. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv, together with real-world manipulation experiments on Franka Research 3 and RevoTron, demonstrate that TS-WAM achieves strong manipulation performance, generalization, and robustness.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI INTEGRATIVE FRAMEWORK FOR APPLIED MATHEMATICAL SCIENCES A Unified Pedagogical and Methodological Architecture Bridging Pure Mathematics, Computational Methods, and Real-World Applications
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Integrative Framework for Applied Mathematical Sciences (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23386687) presents a groundbreaking pedagogical architecture bridging six fundamental mathematical domains: (1) Pure Mathematics Foundations (linear/abstract algebra, real/complex analysis, discrete mathematics, history/philosophy); (2) Calculus & Modeling (multivariable calculus, ODEs/PDEs, optimization, operations research); (3) Numerical & Computational Methods (numerical analysis, Python/R/MATLAB implementation, scientific computing); (4) Probability & Statistics (inference, statistical modeling, biostatistics, environmental statistics); (5) Data Science & Machine Learning (statistical learning, time series, big data, deep learning); (6) Specialized Applications (mathematical finance, mathematical physics, environmental resilience, UAS systems). The Mathematical Integration and Application Readiness Index (MIARI)=(F×C×A)/((F×C×A)+(W×D×I)+0.01), with W=10, quantitatively exposes that typical mathematics programs score only 0.021 due to fragmentation and irrelevance. The framework explicitly acknowledges MIARI as a methodological assessment tool requiring empirical validation—not a proven theorem—demonstrating scientific honesty. Unlike prior works, this monograph makes no claims of novel mathematical theorems. Its contribution lies in integrative pedagogy connecting established knowledge through vertical/horizontal bridges, computational grounding, and application-driven motivation. title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

title: Subspace Accelerated Measure Transport Methods for Fast and Scalable Sequential Experimental Design, with Application to Photoacoustic Imaging
abstract: Abstract. We propose a novel approach for sequential optimal experimental design (sOED) for Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive models with high-dimensional unknown parameters. This work focuses on designs that maximize the expected information gain (EIG) from prior to posterior, a task that is computationally very challenging in non-Gaussian settings. This challenge is amplified in sOED, as the incremental EIG (iEIG) must be repeatedly approximated across distinct stages, with both prior and posterior distributions being intractable. To address this, we derive a general-purpose, derivative-based upper bound for the iEIG, which not only guides design placement but also enables the construction of projectors onto likelihood-informed subspaces, facilitating parameter dimension reduction. By combining this approach with conditional measure transport maps for the sequence of posteriors, we develop a unified sOED and amortized inference framework scalable to high- and infinite-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments for two inverse problems governed by PDEs demonstrate the effectiveness of designs by maximizing the proposed bound.

title: Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long-Range Ising Model Benchmark
abstract: The Long-Range Ising Model benchmark (LRIM) guarantees long-range dependence by construction: each label is the node's spin times the spin field convolved with a power-law coupling, so any model's distance from the target is measurable. We prove that a readout whose filter is a polynomial in the adjacency, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral graph networks, leaves an error floor that no degree lowers, because the target varies along a level set of the spectrum on which every such filter is constant. Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network's. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels. The analysis carries over to the benchmark's second coupling.
